datasets.title: SBI forex card rates, USD TT buy and TT sell
datasets.name: SBI forex card
datasets.summary: What SBI charges to convert between rupees and US dollars on a forex card, per the rate sheet it publishes each banking day. TT buy is what a dollar fetches; TT sell is what a dollar costs.

datasets.title: USD/INR exchange rate, daily, from the BIS
datasets.name: BIS USD/INR
datasets.summary: Rupees per US dollar on each business day since 1973, as the Bank for International Settlements publishes it. A reference rate rather than a price anyone transacts at; SBI's card rates are what a transfer costs.

datasets.title: India CPI, all-India combined, general index
datasets.name: MoSPI CPI
datasets.summary: India's consumer price index for all of India, rural and urban combined, as MoSPI publishes it on its 2024 base. Divide two months' values to get the inflation between them.

published.licence: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, open data

source.text: MoSPI eSankhyiki CPI, base 2024, Back and Current series

datasets.title: India CPI, monthly since 1957, from the IMF
datasets.name: IMF CPI
datasets.summary: India's consumer price index back to 1957, which the IMF builds by linking India's earlier national series onto the 2024 = 100 base. It matches MoSPI's index from 2025; before 2013, it is the only monthly India CPI here.

datasets.title: India central bank policy rate, monthly since 1946, from the BIS
datasets.name: BIS India policy rate
datasets.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's policy rate at the end of each month, as the BIS publishes it: the repo rate from 3 April 2001, and the bank rate before, since the RBI had no single policy rate until then. A rate the central bank sets, not a return anyone earns; market short rates trade near it.

datasets.title: US central bank policy rate, monthly since 1954, from the BIS
datasets.name: BIS US policy rate
datasets.summary: The Federal Reserve's policy rate at the end of each month, as the BIS publishes it: the Fed funds target from 19 December 1985, taking the midpoint once the target became a range in December 2008, and the effective Fed funds rate before. A rate the central bank sets, not a return anyone earns; market short rates trade near it.
